{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Patch testing requires 3 additional visits during screening, increasing patient burden",
      "quote": "Patients will be called to the site for 3 visits for the patch testing",
      "page": 70,
      "section": "9.2.1.1 Patch Testing",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The patch testing adds three unscheduled visits during the screening period, which is already long (D-56 to D-1). This increases patient burden and may impact recruitment and retention.",
      "fix": "Consider consolidating patch test readings or using a single extended visit if feasible, or allow previous patch test results within a longer window to reduce visits."
    },
    {
      "title": "Screening period is long (up to 56 days) with multiple procedures, increasing burden",
      "quote": "V1 D-56 to D-1 (Day -56)",
      "page": 62,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The screening period extends up to 56 days, which is lengthy and may lead to patient dropout or loss of interest. Combined with patch testing visits, this is a significant burden.",
      "fix": "Shorten the screening window if possible, or streamline procedures to reduce the number of visits required."
    },
    {
      "title": "Injection training/observation and administration of study drug are scheduled at every visit from V2 to V9, which may be burdensome",
      "quote": "Injection training/ observation |  |  | X | X | X |  | X |  | X |  |  |  |  |",
      "page": 62,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Injection training/observation and study drug administration occur at V2, V3, V4, V6, V8, and V9 (every 2 weeks). This frequent dosing schedule may be burdensome for patients, especially if they are self-administering.",
      "fix": "Consider reducing the frequency of on-site administration if patients can self-administer at home, or provide training to enable home administration earlier."
    },
    {
      "title": "Patient assessment of hand and foot pruritus intensity using NRS via diary is required daily, which may be burdensome",
      "quote": "Patient assessment of hand and foot pruritus intensity using NRS via diary (daily)",
      "page": 62,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Daily diary completion for pruritus NRS is required from screening through EOS, which is a long duration (over 6 months). This may lead to poor compliance and missing data.",
      "fix": "Consider using electronic diaries with reminders, or reduce the frequency to weekly if clinically acceptable."
    },
    {
      "title": "Con meds/procedures and skin protection measures are recorded at every visit, including unscheduled and ET visits, which may be redundant",
      "quote": "Con meds/procedures | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X | X",
      "page": 62,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Con meds and skin protection measures are collected at every visit, including unscheduled and early termination visits. This is comprehensive but may be redundant if no changes occur; it could be streamlined to reduce data entry burden.",
      "fix": "Consider collecting at specified intervals (e.g., every 4 weeks) and at unscheduled visits only if there is a change."
    },
    {
      "title": "Vital signs and physical examination are not performed at V3, V4, V6, V8, V9, which may be inconsistent with safety monitoring",
      "quote": "Vital signs | X |  | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X | X | X | X",
      "page": 62,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Vital signs and physical exams are only at screening, baseline, EOT, EOS, unscheduled, and ET. They are missing at intermediate visits (V3, V4, V6, V8, V9) where study drug is administered. This could miss safety signals.",
      "fix": "Add vital signs at least at visits where study drug is administered, or justify their omission based on risk assessment."
    },
    {
      "title": "Hematology, chemistry, and urinalysis are not collected at intermediate visits, which may be insufficient for safety monitoring",
      "quote": "Hematology | X |  | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X | X | X | X",
      "page": 62,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Lab tests are only at screening, baseline, EOT, EOS, unscheduled, and ET. No labs at intermediate visits (V3, V4, V6, V8, V9) despite frequent dosing. This may be insufficient to monitor for lab abnormalities.",
      "fix": "Consider adding labs at least at mid-study visits (e.g., V6 or V8) to ensure safety."
    },
    {
      "title": "Photographs of atopic hand or foot dermatitis are only at baseline, EOT, and EOS, which may not capture disease changes over time",
      "quote": "Photograph areas of atopic hand or foot dermatitis (select sites) |  |  | X |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | X | X |  | X",
      "page": 62,
      "section": "Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Photographs are taken only at baseline, EOT, and EOS. This may not adequately document disease progression or response over time, especially for a chronic condition like hand and foot dermatitis.",
      "fix": "Consider adding photographs at intermediate visits (e.g., V4 or V6) to better capture changes."
    }
  ]
}
